summary: MCQ practice app for AIAPGET (All India Ayush Post Graduate Entrance Test) Previous Year Questions (PYQ) focused on Unani System of Medicine. Users can practice multiple choice questions to prepare for the exam.
architectural_notes: App domain: AIAPGET exam prep for Unani System of Medicine
Question format: MCQ (Multiple Choice Questions) with PYQ (Previous Year Questions)
Admin panel password is 'Naeem9472' (hardcoded in frontend)
App is being upgraded to PWA (Progressive Web App) for mobile installability and offline support
known_issues: Admin panel shows 'only admin can add question' message instead of the question submission form
Newly added questions do not appear in their assigned category/topic filter
Submitting a question via the Admin Panel form results in a 'failed to add question' error
Deployment error on go-live for Version 11
Correct answer option text color is not visible after clicking (font color blends with background); correct option text should be bold and use a contrasting color
imageRequirements:
## Required Images
- Circular app icon with Unani medicine motif — ornate geometric arabesque border, central herb/vessel illustration on a deep teal background with gold accents (icon-192.dim_192x192.png)
- Circular app icon with Unani medicine motif — ornate geometric arabesque border, central herb/vessel illustration on a deep teal background with gold accents, high resolution (icon-512.dim_512x512.png)

existing_features.title: Build a home screen with navigation options: Start Practice Quiz, Browse by Topic, Browse by Year, and View Score History. Display the app name and a brief description of the AIAPGET Unani exam.

Build a quiz interface where users answer MCQs one at a time. Each question card shows the question text, four labeled options (A–D), and a question counter (e.g., 'Question 3 of 20'). After selecting an option, the answer is locked and the user can proceed to the next question via a 'Next' button. A progress bar or step indicator must be visible throughout the quiz.

Build a result summary screen shown at the end of each quiz session. Display: total questions attempted, number of correct answers, percentage score, and a pass/fail or performance tier indicator. Include a 'Review Answers' button and a 'Start New Quiz' button.

Build an answer review screen accessible after quiz completion. For each question in the completed quiz, display: the question text, all four options, the user's selected answer (highlighted), and the correct answer (highlighted in green). If available, show a brief explanation or reference for the correct answer.

Build a topic browser screen listing all Unani subject categories. Clicking a category shows all questions under that topic in a list view. Users can start a quiz filtered to only that topic from this screen.

Build a score history screen that fetches and displays all past quiz attempts from the backend. Each record should show the date/time, score (correct/total), and percentage. Display in reverse chronological order.

Apply a cohesive visual theme inspired by classical Unani/Islamic manuscript aesthetics: warm parchment/cream background tones, deep teal and gold accent colors, elegant serif or calligraphic-style headings paired with clean sans-serif body text, and subtle geometric/arabesque decorative elements. Enforce this theme consistently across all screens.

Generate and use a decorative banner/hero image for the home screen representing the Unani system of medicine — herbs, traditional medicine vessels, and manuscript motifs — and an app logo/icon. Render these as static assets from frontend/public/assets/generated.

Diagnose and fix the deployment error that occurred in the most recent build. Ensure the Motoko backend actor compiles without errors, all backend query and update functions are syntactically correct and type-safe, and the frontend builds successfully with no TypeScript or import errors.

Build an Admin Panel screen accessible from the home screen (e.g., via an 'Admin' button or link). The panel must contain a form allowing submission of a new MCQ question with the following fields: question text (textarea), four answer options (Option A–D), correct answer selector (radio or dropdown), topic/subject category (dropdown populated with existing Unani topic constants), and exam year (input or dropdown). On submission, call the backend `addQuestion` function and show a success or error notification. The screen must also list all existing questions with their topic and year for admin review.

Remove or bypass the role-based access guard on the Admin Panel screen so that any user (not just a designated admin principal) can see and use the question submission form. The 'only admin can add question' gate should be removed from the frontend UI, allowing all visitors to access the add-question form and the existing question list without restriction.

Fix the frontend Topic Browser screen (`TopicBrowserScreen.tsx`) and any other screens that filter questions by topic or year to also include questions fetched from the backend (via `getAdminQuestions` or the unified question query), not only the local static `questions.ts` data. The topic/category filter UI must merge backend-stored questions with the local question bank so that admin-added questions are visible in the topic browser and year browser.

Fix the Admin Panel screen (`AdminPanelScreen.tsx`) 'Questions in Database' section so that it displays admin-added questions fetched from the backend without showing an unauthorized error. The frontend must call `getAdminQuestions` without any role guard that blocks the request, ensuring all users see the question list.

Remove the 'only admin can add question' restriction from the frontend AdminPanelScreen.tsx so that the question submission form is visible and usable by all visitors without any role or identity check. Any remaining UI guard, conditional render, or access check that hides the form behind an admin role must be eliminated.

Add a password prompt/gate in AdminPanelScreen.tsx that must be completed before the add-question form is shown. The screen should display a password input field and a 'Submit' button when the user first opens the Admin Panel. Only after the user enters the correct hardcoded admin password (e.g., 'unani2024') should the question submission form and the questions list become visible. If the password is incorrect, show an inline error message. The unlocked state should persist for the duration of the session (e.g., stored in component state) but reset when the user navigates away from the screen.

In AdminPanelScreen.tsx, update the hardcoded admin password used by the password gate from the current value (e.g., 'unani2024') to 'Naeem9472'. The password prompt, error message on wrong input, and unlock behaviour must remain unchanged — only the accepted password string changes.

Diagnose and fix the 'Failed to add question' error that occurs when submitting the Add Question form in AdminPanelScreen.tsx. Inspect the backend `addQuestion` update function in backend/main.mo and ensure it accepts calls from any caller (authenticated or anonymous) without throwing an authorization or role error. Verify the function signature, parameter types, and return type are correct and match what the frontend hook `useAddQuestion` sends. The form submission must succeed and return a success notification to the user.

After fixing the backend `addQuestion` function, verify and update the frontend `useAddQuestion` mutation hook in `frontend/src/hooks/useAdminQueries.ts` to ensure the argument object it sends matches the exact field names and types now accepted by the backend. If any field mapping is mismatched (e.g., `correctAnswer` vs `correctAnswerIndex`, numeric vs text year), correct the frontend payload construction so the call succeeds without a type mismatch rejection.

Ensure the frontend builds successfully with no TypeScript compilation errors or import errors, so that the full deployment pipeline (backend canister + frontend asset bundle) completes without failure.

Add a subscription plans screen accessible from the app. The screen must display two plan options: Monthly Subscription and Yearly Subscription. Each plan card should clearly show the plan name, price, billing cycle, and a list of included benefits. The yearly plan should highlight savings compared to the monthly plan (e.g., 'Save 20%'). Include a 'Subscribe' or 'Get Started' button on each plan card.

On the subscription plans screen, display a payment methods section listing all supported payment methods: UPI, Credit Card, Debit Card, Net Banking, and Wallets. Each method should be shown with a recognizable icon or label. The UPI option must be prominently listed. When a user selects a plan and clicks Subscribe, they should be shown a payment method selector UI (no actual transaction processing required — UI flow only).

Add a 3-dot vertical kebab menu button in the top-left corner of the home screen header, styled like a professional mobile app. Tapping the button opens a slide-out drawer or dropdown menu containing navigation links: Home, Practice Quiz, Browse by Topic, Browse by Year, Score History, Subscription Plans, and Admin Panel. The menu must be dismissible by tapping outside or pressing a close button. Apply the existing parchment/teal/gold theme to the menu.

In TopicBrowserScreen.tsx, identify the color/style applied to the 'Start Quiz' button rendered in the Browse by Topic section, then apply that exact same color, background, border, and hover styling to the equivalent 'Start Quiz' (or quiz launch) button rendered in the Browse by Year section, so both sections are visually consistent.

In QuizScreen.tsx, fix the correct answer option so that after the user clicks and the answer is revealed, the text label of the correct option is displayed in a clearly visible, high-contrast font color (e.g., dark text such as deep teal or dark green, not white-on-white or invisible) and is rendered in bold. The image shows that option B is highlighted with a teal/green background and border but the option text is invisible — this must be corrected so the text is legible against the highlighted background. Apply the same fix to ReviewScreen.tsx wherever the correct answer option is highlighted.

In the Admin Panel add-question form in `AdminPanelScreen.tsx`, add an optional 'Explanation' text field (textarea) below the correct answer selector. The field should be clearly labelled 'Explanation (optional)' and its value must be submitted alongside the other question fields when the form is submitted.

Update the `useAddQuestion` mutation hook in `frontend/src/hooks/useAdminQueries.ts` to include the optional `explanation` field in the payload it sends to the backend. If the form's explanation field is empty, send an empty optional value (matching the backend's `?Text` type).

In `AdminPanelScreen.tsx`, update the exam year dropdown to include all years from 2016 to the current year (inclusive), generated dynamically so it always includes the present year without requiring code changes in future years.

In `AdminPanelScreen.tsx`, remove any frontend-side error display, conditional render, or access check that shows the 'Unauthorized: Only admins can add questions' message or hides the Add Question form behind a role check. The password gate (password: 'Naeem9472') must remain as the only gate. Once the correct password is entered, the Add Question form and the Questions list must both be fully visible and functional with no unauthorized error shown.

Convert the frontend into a Progressive Web App (PWA) by adding a Web App Manifest file (manifest.json or manifest.webmanifest) in the frontend/public directory. The manifest must include: app name ('AIAPGET Unani PYQ Practice'), short name ('Unani PYQ'), start URL, display mode 'standalone', background color matching the parchment theme (e.g., #f5f0e8), theme color matching the deep teal accent, and icon references for at least 192x192 and 512x512 sizes. Reference the manifest in frontend/index.html via a <link rel='manifest'> tag.

Register a Service Worker in the frontend to enable offline support and caching. The service worker must cache all critical static assets (HTML, JS, CSS, images) on install so the app loads when the device is offline. Use a cache-first strategy for static assets and a network-first strategy for API/canister calls. Register the service worker in frontend/src/main.tsx or via a separate registration script loaded in frontend/index.html.

Add PWA icon assets for the home screen and splash screen. Generate a 192x192 and a 512x512 version of the app icon (based on the existing app logo/Unani motif) and place them at frontend/public/assets/generated/icon-192.png and frontend/public/assets/generated/icon-512.png respectively. Reference these paths in the manifest icons array.

Add the necessary meta tags to frontend/index.html for iOS PWA support: apple-mobile-web-app-capable, apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style (set to 'black-translucent' or matching the teal theme), apple-mobile-web-app-title, and apple-touch-icon pointing to the 192x192 icon. Also set the <meta name='theme-color'> to match the app's deep teal accent color so the browser toolbar matches the app theme on Android.

new_feature_requests.summary: MCQ quiz interface for AIAPGET PYQ questions on Unani medicine
Question bank with previous year questions categorized by topic/year
Score tracking and result summary after each quiz session
Answer review with explanations after quiz completion

Create a backend Motoko actor with a question bank data structure containing at least 50 AIAPGET previous year MCQs specific to the Unani System of Medicine. Each question must include: question text, four answer options (A–D), correct answer index, topic/subject category (e.g., Kulliyat, Ilmul Advia, Moalijat, Tashreeh, etc.), and year of the exam.

Implement backend query functions: get all questions, get questions filtered by topic, get questions filtered by year, and get a randomized quiz set of N questions. Also implement an update function to record user quiz attempt scores (total questions, correct answers, timestamp).
Admin panel to add/manage questions, with options to assign year and topic/subject category to each question

Extend the Motoko backend actor to support admin question management: add an update function `addQuestion` that accepts a full question record (question text, four answer options, correct answer index, topic/subject category, year) and appends it to the persistent question bank. Add a query function `getAdminQuestions` to retrieve all questions for admin review. Ensure type safety and that existing query functions (getQuestions, getByTopic, getByYear, recordAttempt) continue to work correctly.

Remove or relax the admin-only guard on the backend `addQuestion` update function so that any caller can invoke it without being rejected due to role restrictions. Ensure `getAdminQuestions` also remains accessible without a role check.

Fix the backend so that questions added via the `addQuestion` update function are included in the results returned by `getByTopic` and `getByYear` query functions. Currently, admin-added questions are stored separately and are not merged into the main question bank that category/topic filters query against. The backend must unify all questions (both hardcoded and admin-added) into a single source that all query functions (`getQuestions`, `getByTopic`, `getByYear`, and the random quiz set function) draw from.

Remove the authorization check on the backend `getAdminQuestions` query function so that any caller (authenticated or anonymous) can retrieve admin-added questions without receiving an 'Unauthorized: Only admins can access admin questions' error. The function must return all stored admin questions to all callers without a role check.

Remove the authorization/role check from the backend addQuestion update function in backend/main.mo so that any caller (authenticated or anonymous) can invoke it without being rejected. Also ensure getAdminQuestions has no role guard and returns all stored questions to any caller.
Add an admin password prompt/gate before allowing question submission in the Admin Panel. Users must enter a correct password before the add-question form becomes accessible.

Diagnose and fix the IC0508 canister rejection error thrown by the backend `addQuestion` update function. The error shown is a 'non_replicated_rejection' with reject code 5, meaning the canister is trapping or throwing during execution. Rewrite the `addQuestion` function in backend/main.mo so it: (1) removes any remaining authorization/role/caller check that could cause a trap, (2) uses only stable or correctly typed mutable state for storing questions, (3) accepts the question record with exactly the field types the frontend sends (text fields as Text, correctAnswer as Nat, topic as Text, year as Text or Nat as appropriate), and (4) returns a simple success/error variant or Bool without any guard that would reject anonymous callers. Ensure the function compiles cleanly and does not trap at runtime under any caller identity.

Diagnose and fix the deployment error that caused the Version 11 go-live to fail. Audit the Motoko backend (backend/main.mo) for any compilation errors, type mismatches, or runtime traps — particularly in the `addQuestion` and `getAdminQuestions` functions — and resolve them so the canister compiles and deploys successfully.
Add monthly and yearly subscription options with all payment methods including UPI. Add a 3-dot menu (hamburger/kebab) in the top-left corner like a professional app.

Add a backend data structure and functions to store subscription plan definitions (plan name, price, billing cycle, features list) as stable state in backend/main.mo. Expose a query function `getSubscriptionPlans` that returns all available plans. No payment processing logic is required — only plan metadata storage and retrieval.
Fix the 'Browse by Year' section so that the quiz option button/card color matches the styling used in the 'Browse by Topic' section.

Fix the correct answer option text color visibility after clicking — the font color is not visible when the correct option is selected/revealed. Change the font color to be clearly visible and make the correct option text bold.
In the Admin Panel add-question form, add an optional 'Explanation' field for the correct answer. Also update the exam year dropdown/input to include years from 2016 to the current year.

Update the backend `addQuestion` function in `backend/main.mo` to accept an optional `explanation` field (type `?Text`) in the question record. Ensure that existing stored questions without an explanation remain valid, and that the explanation value is stored and returned by `getAdminQuestions`.

Remove the 'Unauthorized: Only admins can add questions' error banner from the Admin Panel screen. The backend `addQuestion` update function in `backend/main.mo` must accept calls from any caller (authenticated or anonymous) without performing any role or principal check that causes a rejection or trap. Remove all authorization guards from both `addQuestion` and `getAdminQuestions` in the backend so they are fully open to any caller.
Upgrade the app to a Progressive Web App (PWA) with offline support, splash screen, and native app feel so users can install it on mobile devices from their browser.
